assigned.title: The screen the operator is looking at is the only one that cannot say what failed
assigned.acceptance:
THE SYMPTOM, FROM THE OPERATOR'S INSTALLED MSI AT f02703e. Windows package, desktop shell and CI all pass. The MSI installs, the native window opens, the bundled node starts, and the handshake completes -- liberty-sidecar-ready {"host":"127.0.0.1","port":62699}, followed by "catalog metadata source: none requested", which proves instrumentation ran to completion and the sidecar process is healthy. The window then displays:

  Project Liberty could not start this page
  Something failed before the application frame could render.

THAT TEXT IS apps/web/src/app/global-error.tsx, AND IT IS THE ONE SCREEN IN THIS APPLICATION THAT CANNOT SAY WHAT WENT WRONG. The component's signature was `{ reset }` -- it never declared Next's `error` argument, so the error was dropped at the parameter list. It logged nothing. It showed no digest. And its own comment said "The log has it", which was FALSE: nothing anywhere wrote it. Three rounds of Windows work were spent guessing at a failure that was reporting itself to nobody.

WHAT ITS PRESENCE ALREADY TELLS US, AND IT NARROWS THE PROBLEM A LOT. global-error renders only when the render fails at or above the root layout. For the operator to be looking at it, the window had ALREADY navigated to the sidecar origin, the document request had ALREADY passed the 403 request guard, and Next had ALREADY served HTML. So this is not PL-0753's class and not the shell's supervision path -- surface_failure drives the bundled splash, which contains none of this text. It is a render or hydration failure inside the application.

WHAT THIS TASK DOES NOT DO, STATED FIRST BECAUSE IT IS THE HONEST SHAPE OF IT: it does not fix the render failure. The failure cannot be identified from this session. The packaged production artifact was booted here and GET / answers 200 with the real application -- the app shell, the skip link, the navigation including Browse, 2 inline scripts and 10 script tags all carrying a CSP nonce. So the defect does not reproduce on Linux from the same tree, and nothing records it on Windows. This task makes it RECORD ITSELF, which is the only thing that can end the guessing.

REQUIRED: THE BOUNDARY RECEIVES THE ERROR AND SURFACES THE DIGEST. The existing reasoning was half right -- a root-layout failure can carry a stack trace and a digest is the only thing safe to show. It then omitted the digest too. A digest is Next's own correlation id, lowercase hex, no message and no path; showing it is what lets an operator quote one line that matches a line in the log. When Next minted none, the page says so rather than leaving a blank where a reference should be.

REQUIRED: THE REPORT REACHES THE FILE THE OPERATOR ALREADY PASTES. The Rust shell captures the sidecar's stdout and stderr, redacts tokens, budget-caps the volume and writes %LOCALAPPDATA%\app.projectliberty.desktop\logs\sidecar.log. A browser-side failure had no route into it -- console.error in the page goes to the webview's console, which nothing captures. One POST to a local diagnostics route closes the gap and adds no file, no port and no new place to look.

REQUIRED: NO MESSAGE AND NO STACK CROSS THAT BOUNDARY. A message from a server component can carry a file path, a connection string, a query or a token; a stack carries build paths. The report is five bounded fields -- boundary, pathname with the query and fragment REMOVED, digest matched against lowercase hex, error name matched against an identifier pattern, and hadMessage as a BOOLEAN so a reader can tell an error that said nothing from one whose text was withheld. The server re-sanitises with the same rules rather than believing a body because it came from our own page.

REQUIRED: THE REPORTER CANNOT BE THE FAILURE. It is called from the last-resort boundary, which must not import the shell, the stylesheet, or anything that could be what just failed. The module imports NOTHING -- no React, no CSS, no contract package -- is total against anything JavaScript can throw including a throwing getter, and swallows every failure of its own.

REQUIRED: A REFUSAL LEAVES A TRACE. The request guard answers 403 with no body and no reason, deliberately, so the wire cannot be used as an oracle for which check failed -- and the consequence nobody accounted for is that a refusal left no trace ANYWHERE, which is why "does the installed WebView get 200 or 403" was unanswerable from the machine that served it. The wire is unchanged. The server-side log records the method, the path without its query, and whether a token header and a Host header were PRESENT -- no header value, and not which check failed. Between them those separate a webview that never attaches the token from one that attaches it to some requests and not others, from a Host mismatch, from a request that is not ours.

REQUIRED: BOTH LOGS ARE BUDGETED. One refused page load is dozens of refusals and a remount loop reports continuously; the line that matters is the first one. The budget keeps the first few per window, drops the rest, and says once per window how many it dropped -- so the log states that it stopped recording rather than appearing to say the failures stopped.

MUST NOT: weaken the request guard, change what the wire says, widen what the 403 reveals, or record any header value, token, query string or user data.

MUST NOT: claim the startup failure is fixed. It is not diagnosed. What this earns is that the next MSI run will say what failed, in the file the operator already sends.
assigned.notes: FILED 2026-10-11 from the Wave 131 operator report. Two recon findings were checked and REJECTED before this was written: that the packaged proxy fails to forward a CSP nonce (the live packaged response carries a nonce on all 12 script tags), and that the homepage is served as an error page on Linux (it is the real application, 200). Both came from subagent reads of prerendered build output rather than of a live response.

typecheck.evidence:
TYPECHECK, at 52213cf26a4c57572a99e6044f4a9c6b878d3090.

npm run typecheck (turbo, whole repository): 22 tasks successful, 22 total. npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/web clean. npm run repo:validate passed. npm run ai:validate: 159 tasks, 9 agents. npx eslint . --ignore-pattern "dist/**" in apps/web: 0 errors, 2 warnings, both pre-existing in files this change does not touch (api/v1/profiles/preferences/handler.test.ts, lib/db/in-memory-repository.test.ts). A third warning was mine -- an import left unused after two tests were removed -- and it is gone.

AND THE ROUTE COMPILES AS A ROUTE. npm run build:desktop -w @liberty/web lists /api/v1/diagnostics/client-failure in its route table. A diagnostics endpoint that type-checks but does not register would be the exact failure mode this task exists to remove.

TWO RECON FINDINGS WERE CHECKED AND REJECTED BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN, and recording that is part of the evidence because both would have sent this round somewhere wrong.

(1) "proxy.ts mints a CSP nonce but never forwards it into the request headers, so every inline Next script is CSP-blocked in the installed build." Measured instead: the packaged production artifact was booted and GET / inspected. The response CSP is script-src 'self' 'nonce-<32 hex>'; the body carries 2 inline <script> tags and 10 <script src> tags, and ALL TWELVE carry nonce=. The finding came from reading the PRERENDERED _global-error.html, which has no nonce because it was rendered at build time with no request. Not a defect.

(2) The implied reading that the homepage is served as an error page. Measured: GET / is 200, 15378 bytes, and contains skip-link, class="shell", the nav with Browse/Search/Watchlist, and the catalog state panel. It does NOT contain "could not start this page". So the operator's failure does not reproduce on Linux from this tree.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED ABOUT THE OPERATOR'S FAILURE, AND IT IS NARROWER THAN A FIX. The text is apps/web/src/app/global-error.tsx, which Next renders only when the render fails at or above the root layout. For it to be on screen: the window had navigated to the sidecar origin, the document request had passed the 403 guard, and Next had served HTML. So it is not PL-0753's 403 class, and not the shell's supervision path -- surface_failure drives apps/desktop/dist/index.html, which contains none of this wording. It is a render or hydration failure inside the application, on Windows, that does not occur here.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: which failure. I did not identify it and this task does not claim to. The reason it could not be identified is the thing being fixed: the boundary took only `reset`, so Next's `error` argument was dropped at the parameter list; it logged nothing; it showed no digest; and its comment said "The log has it" while nothing wrote it.

unit.evidence:
UNIT, at 52213cf26a4c57572a99e6044f4a9c6b878d3090.

npx vitest run --root apps/web: 100 files, 1772 tests, all passing, 71.0s. 37 are new: lib/diagnostics/client-failure.test.ts (21), app/api/v1/diagnostics/client-failure/handler.test.ts (8), lib/diagnostics/refusal-log.test.ts (8)... counted precisely: 32 across those three files plus 6 in app/error-boundaries.test.tsx, 38 in total, and the suite moved from 1735 to 1772 because one pre-existing file is unchanged in count.

WHAT THE REPORTER'S TESTS PIN, and the first two are the security properties:
  - NO MESSAGE AND NO STACK CAN TRAVEL. An error whose message is "postgres://user:pw@host/db" produces a report whose serialisation contains neither "postgres" nor "pw@host", and whose key set is exactly boundary/digest/errorName/hadMessage/pathname.
  - THE QUERY IS DROPPED, NOT TRUNCATED: /search?q=secret+thing becomes /search, and /browse?kind=series&genre=Drama becomes /browse. A diagnostic has no business recording what a viewer typed. The fragment goes too.
  - A digest that is not a digest is refused rather than laundered: "../../etc/passwd", an uppercased digest, a hyphenated one, an empty one and an over-long one all become null. Same for an error name that is not an identifier.
  - TOTALITY, because this is called from the last-resort boundary and JavaScript can throw anything: null, undefined, a string, a number, a Symbol and an array all produce a valid report, and an object whose `digest` getter THROWS does not propagate.
  - The server re-sanitises rather than trusting a body because it shares its origin: a POST claiming digest "NOT A DIGEST", a query-bearing pathname and hadMessage "yes" is normalised to null/stripped/false, and extra `stack` and `message` fields are dropped rather than logged.

THE ROUTE'S TESTS pin the bound, the budget and the silence: an oversized body is refused 413 BEFORE anything parses it (request.text() then measure, because request.json() on an unmeasured body parses whatever arrived); a non-report is 400 and logs nothing; the FIRST reports in a window are kept and the rest dropped, because the tenth copy of a failure says nothing the first did not; a dropped report still answers 204 so the wire says nothing about the budget; and the count of dropped reports is stated once when the next window opens and not again.

THE REFUSAL LOG'S TESTS pin that no header VALUE is recorded, that the query is stripped from the path, that an unusual method is normalised to OTHER rather than echoed, and that the token-present/absent pair -- the distinction that made PL-0753 diagnosable only from an operator's screenshot -- is what the line carries.

THE BOUNDARY TESTS CARRY A PREMISE FOR ANOTHER WORKSPACE'S CHECK, and that is the interesting one. PL-0755's smoke test now requires AppShell's markers in the homepage and refuses the error headline. That assertion is only worth anything while the error page is distinguishable from a working one -- a fact about global-error.tsx, which that script cannot import because it runs against a packaged tree with no TypeScript. So app/error-boundaries.test.tsx asserts global-error carries the headline and NONE of skip-link, class="shell" or id="main". MUTANT RUN: adding a skip link and id="main" to global-error fails that test with 'global-error must not emit skip-link; the smoke test depends on it'. Reverted; 6/6 green.

TWO TESTS WERE WRITTEN, FAILED, AND REMOVED RATHER THAN PROPPED UP. error.tsx renders AppShell, which contains next/link; rendering a "use client" component through renderToStaticMarkup puts that Link in a client tree with no app-router context and React fails with "invariant expected app router to be mounted". profile-ui.test.tsx renders the same AppShell successfully because it renders it from a SERVER tree. apps/web/vitest.config.ts is environment: "node" with no jsdom and no router mock, so there is nowhere to mount one. Adding a mock would have made this file the only place in the suite that fakes Next's internals. The reason is written in the file where the tests were. What covers that boundary instead: the shared reporter it calls, tested directly; its digest line, unchanged since PW-0301; and Playwright, which this session cannot execute.

NOT CLAIMED: that the installed application now starts. It is not diagnosed. What this earns is that the next MSI run writes what failed into %LOCALAPPDATA%\app.projectliberty.desktop\logs\sidecar.log -- a liberty-client-failure line with the boundary, the route and the digest, and a liberty-request-refused line for any refusal -- in the file the operator already pastes. The operator validation procedure is in the apply script.

assigned.title: There is no way to browse the catalog: home shows two rails and search needs you to know the answer
assigned.acceptance:
THE GAP. docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md names "Home/catalog/search" among the MVP capabilities. Home and search exist; there is no catalog surface. Browsing is currently two home rails -- RAIL_DEFINITIONS in lib/catalog.ts, films and series, newest first -- plus a search box that requires the viewer to already know what they are looking for. A viewer who wants to see what is in the catalog, or everything in one genre, has nowhere to go. /browse, /catalog, components/browse and any live-TV route do not exist in apps/web/src/app.

REQUIRED: A BROWSE SURFACE THAT READS THE SAME PORT THROUGH THE SAME GATES. The catalog metadata port (lib/catalog-source-registry.ts), then selectDeclaredItems, then isSurfaceable, then the browsable-kind allowlist -- the order home and search both already apply, and in that order, so a record whose rights basis the source did not declare is never reachable from this surface either. No new provider, no new fixture, no second catalog read path.

REQUIRED: THE FACETS ARE DERIVED FROM WHAT SURVIVED THE RIGHTS GATE, NOT FROM THE RECORDS. A genre list is published to the reader. Deriving it before the gate would let a withheld record contribute a genre name -- disclosing that the catalog holds something of that kind while refusing to show it, which is a rights leak through a filter control rather than through a card. The facet list must be computed from the surfaced items only, and a test must pin that ORDERING. The test needs a cast to do it, and the cast is itself the finding: contentRightsSchema admits only the three playable values, so every schema-valid CatalogItem is surfaceable and the union cannot express a withheld one -- the real withholding happens upstream in selectDeclaredItems, which refuses a record before it becomes an item at all. The ordering is still load-bearing against the rights vocabulary being widened later, which is the only way it can regress, and the test says so rather than implying the type system proves it.

REQUIRED: 'YOUR FILTERS MATCHED NOTHING' AND 'THE CATALOG HAS NOTHING' ARE DIFFERENT PAGES. This is the collapse app/search/search.ts documents at length and lib/catalog.ts carries a cause field for. An empty browse result must say which of the two it is, and the cause must come from the catalog rather than be inferred from the length of a filtered array, because both states legitimately produce an empty array.

REQUIRED: DETERMINISTIC ORDER WITH A FINAL TIEBREAK, AND NO localeCompare. Same catalog and same filters in, same list out, on any host. localeCompare without an explicit locale uses the host's collation, which is the defect already removed from candidate ranking in @liberty/media-engine and from search's result sort; buildHomeCatalog still has it and is not this task's surface. id decides last, so the sort can never fall back on the order the catalog arrived in.

REQUIRED: THE FILTERS LIVE IN THE URL AND WORK WITHOUT JAVASCRIPT. A GET form and search params, so a filtered view is shareable and bookmarkable and so the surface is complete before hydration. Parameters arrive as untrusted input and are read defensively: a repeated parameter takes its first value rather than being joined, an unrecognised value falls back to the unfiltered default, and nothing malformed produces a 500 -- the rules readSearchQueryParam already states for q.

REQUIRED: THE NAVIGATION ENTRY, AND A GUARD THAT THE PROMISE IN THAT FILE IS KEPT. navigation.ts's header says "every entry goes somewhere that exists" and nothing checks it: the existing test only asserts that a live href starts with a slash. A live entry whose route file is absent is exactly the dead link that file was written to remove, so the guard must resolve each live href to a page under apps/web/src/app and fail when one is missing.

MUST NOT: add a play affordance to a browse card, imply a resolvable stream from an item being visible, or weaken any rights gate. Browse is discovery; a stream is resolved through authorized provider adapters at playback time.

MUST NOT: add an HTTP contract or a route handler. docs/API_CONTRACTS.md requires schemas in @liberty/contracts before a route exists, and it lists no browse route among the planned contracts. This value is computed in the server render and nothing transports it, so a wire contract would be contract machinery with no transport. GET /api/v1/search is the planned route that would change that, and it is not this task.

MUST NOT: claim e2e coverage that was not run. The Playwright suite cannot be executed in this session; the surface is covered by vitest, the route is reachable through the navigation guard, and the e2e spec is deliberately left to a task that can run it rather than shipped unexecuted into a 45-minute job.

REQUIRED, ADDED MID-IMPLEMENTATION AND DELIBERATELY RATHER THAN QUIETLY: a brittle count in a test that is not this surface's must become the property it stands for. apps/web/src/components/profiles/profile-ui.test.tsx asserts PRIMARY_NAVIGATION has LENGTH 5 to mean "identity is not a content destination", and the line beside it already asserts that properly by checking /profiles is absent. The count is a proxy that fails on every legitimate nav addition -- it failed on this one -- and replacing it with the property removes a false alarm without removing a guard. The file was added to allowedPaths for this and nothing else; the /profiles assertion stays.

This gate replaces the one recorded earlier for the /browse work alone; the task was reopened from REVIEW with ai:start, which preserves implementationBaseSha, because Wave 131B's Workstream B asks for the existing browse work to be EXTENDED rather than rebuilt and that is this task continuing.

AND THE ROUTES COMPILE AS ROUTES, which a typecheck cannot establish. npm run build:desktop -w @liberty/web lists /browse, /movies and /tv in its route table, all three dynamic -- which is what `export const revalidate = 0` asks for and what a page whose filters live in the URL requires. A prerendered /movies would serve one genre's films at every other genre's address.
